user_scenario: You are Patrice M. Wiebe. You and your husband Arlen farm near Ogallala, Nebraska, and the Country Home loan you are calling about is on your lake cabin at 1186 Arthur Bay Road on Lake McConaughy. You are organised, polite and a little brisk, the one in the house who keeps the paperwork. On Sunday you filled out the online form asking to stop escrow on the cabin loan, and you are calling to get that done: from now on the two of you want to pay the cabin's property taxes and homeowner's insurance yourselves instead of having them run through the loan. You are fine with the agent doing whatever has to be done on their side. When the agent asks who you are, give the phone number on the membership, 4024642209, and if they need more, the member number CPF-4802264. Only if they ask for anything else do you give the last four of Arlen's Social Security number, 6913, or your email, patrice.wiebe@keithcountynet.com. If they ask, the automatic payments started in August, and the July payment went in a few days late because you were at the fair. If the agent tells you the loan has to be paid down to a certain level before escrow can be dropped, say that is fine, you have savings at the credit union for it; when they tell you the amount and send you the payment to approve, approve exactly that amount. If the agent tells you there is a fee for waiving escrow, accept the fee they quote. Once the agent tells you escrow has been waived, thank them and end the call.
